sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球供应链制造母港、跨境电商货源地与外资合规准入市场

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Public Commercial Web Scraping and Proxy API Gateways

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Hong Kong SAR (investor holding jurisdiction); substantive WFOE incorporation in mainland China
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid - mainland China practices civil law; Hong Kong SAR operates a separate common law system
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Mainland and Hong Kong Closer Economic Partnership Arrangement (CEPA), including the Investment Agreement under CEPA
Arrangement between the Mainland of China and the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with respect to Taxes on Income

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: PRC Anti-Money Laundering Law (2024 Revision), effective 1 January 2025; PBOC/SAMR Order No. 3 [2024], Beneficial Owner Information Registration and Administration Measures, effective 1 November 2024; Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 Revision); Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (2019); Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China Articles 191 and 312; and, for the Hong Kong parent holding

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Law of the People’s Republic of China (2023 Revision, effective July 1, 2024), applicable provisions on incorporation of limited liability companies, share capital subscription, articles of association, registered office, officers, and the five-year paid-in capital rule; Foreign Investment Law of the People’s Republic of China (effective January 1, 2020) and its Implementation Regulations, including the negative-list review and Foreign Investment Information Report regime.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation of the People’s Republic of China, acting through the local Market Supervision Administration of the city/district where the Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise’s registered office is located, on the integrated government service online portal for enterprise registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Establishment Registration of a Wholly Foreign-Owned Limited Liability Company, together with the approved Articles of Association and the Initial Foreign Investment Information Report.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. No statutory minimum registered capital and no blocked escrow account are imposed on an ordinary digital-service WFOE. The Hong Kong shareholder shall determine the registered capital in the Articles of Association

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (STA) and the local competent tax office where the WFOE is registered; electronic portal: National Electronic Tax Bureau (e-Tax) via www.chinatax.gov.cn
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Upon incorporation, the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) issues the WFOE a business license with a Unified Social Credit Code (USCC), which is the statutory taxpayer identification number for all PRC tax filings. The WFOE must complete tax registration on the National Electronic Tax Bureau within 30 days of the business license date, submitting the business license, articles of association, registered address proof, legal representative identification, equity structure, and bank account details; the STA then activates the USCC for Enterprise Income Tax, VAT, withholding tax and invoice issuance. A foreign non-resident enterprise (e.g. the Hong Kong parent) with no PRC establishment but deriving China-source income is not separately VAT-registered; the Chinese payer or withholding agent must file the contract withholding registration on the e-Tax platform, where the non-resident is assigned a non-resident tax reference number and the Hong Kong Business Registration number is recorded as the foreign TIN.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The PRC Enterprise Income Tax Law does not provide check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch elections; a WFOE limited-liability entity is mandatorily taxed as a PRC resident enterprise at entity level.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Tax registration is mandatory upon issuance of the SAMR business license. The turnover threshold requiring general VAT taxpayer registration is RMB 5,000,000 in a consecutive 12-month period; below this threshold the WFOE may be treated as a small-scale taxpayer, but general VAT taxpayer status is necessary for the WFOE to issue 0% export VAT invoices for cross-border data/API services and to claim input VAT credits.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China operates the Golden Tax Phase IV system on the National Electronic Tax Bureau. The WFOE must issue Special VAT Invoices or fully digitalised electronic invoices through the official e-invoice platform; each invoice carries a unique invoice code and is transmitted in near real time to the STA. Special VAT invoices must be cleared through the VAT invoice verification platform before input VAT credit is claimed. Anti-fraud controls include automatic transaction matching, risk scoring, abnormal-invoice blocking, and post-export verification of 0% invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The WFOE may claim 0% VAT on export goods and on qualifying cross-border taxable services, including information technology, software, and data-processing services such as commercial web scraping and proxy API gateways, if the recipient is an overseas enterprise or individual, the service is wholly consumed outside Mainland China, the contract and commercial documentation clearly demonstrate offshore supply, and the consideration is received from outside China. The claim is supported by the STA cross-border taxable service zero-rating/exemption framework; the transaction must be recorded as a zero-rated export in the VAT filing and the WFOE must not issue a domestic taxable VAT invoice for the offshore supply.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: PRC Export Customs Declaration (export cargo release record from the China Customs Single Window)
Bill of Lading (ocean) or Air Waybill (air) evidencing physical export of goods
Cross-border service or sales contract identifying the offshore recipient, place of supply, and service scope
Bank receipt of export proceeds in foreign exchange issued by a SAFE-designated bank confirming offshore payment receipt and repatriation
Export VAT rebate declaration e-filing record generated on the State Taxation Administration export tax rebate system
For digital API services: overseas recipient register, service consumption evidence, and SWIFT/Stripe/USDC settlement trail demonstrating foreign exchange repatriation
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Unsubstantiated or false 0% VAT export claims expose the WFOE to retrospective clawback of the VAT refund/exemption, late payment surcharge of 0.05% per day, and administrative penalties of 50% to 500% of the underpaid tax under the PRC Tax Collection Administration Law; fraudulent export-rebate claims involving forged customs or foreign-exchange documents are also punishable under the PRC Customs Law and criminal law, with fines and imprisonment for responsible officers.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC) via the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: RMB is fully convertible for current account transactions including trade in goods and services, but remains heavily regulated on capital account transactions. For a Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise (WFOE) operating in China, foreign currency capital injections from the Hong Kong shareholder must flow through a designated domestic bank under a SAFE foreign exchange registration, and once the funds are credited to the capital escrow account, conversion to RMB is permissible for expenditure within the registered business scope. Profit remittances are permitted after annual audits, tax clearance, and proof that the relevant foreign exchange capital has been paid-up and verified, but require a board resolution and the submission of a Certificate of Payment and Foreign Exchange Verification Form. The WFOE must also comply with the Foreign Exchange Control Regulation and the Administration of Settlement and Sales of Foreign Exchange Provisions, in particular using the correct payment purpose codes. In practice, capital account convertibility is subject to a case-by-case SAFE review, making pre-deal regulatory consultation essential. The strategic use of the Hong Kong jurisdiction as a treasury hub mitigates some restrictions because it provides access to offshore liquidity and hedging markets while the onshore WFOE maintains its own legal capital and operational FX accounts.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Pursuant to SAFE's Export Proceeds Repatriation Administration Provisions, export-related foreign exchange receipts must be repatriated into China through a designated bank within 90 days of the export customs declaration date. The mandatory conversion ratio is effectively zero—exporters may retain the foreign exchange in a Foreign Exchange Settlement Account or convert to RMB at will, provided the balance remains within the approved current account quota. A foreign exchange verification, based on the customs declaration, commercial invoice and bill of lading, is required to close the export collection record. Administrative penalties and potential KYC downgrade apply if repatriation deadlines are missed.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited (ICBC)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Operational Currency Account and Foreign Exchange Settlement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Cross-border fintech electronic money institutions (EMIs) such as Airwallex, Currenxie, or Revolut Business are legally barred from providing onshore banking services or domestic currency accounts to PRC-domiciled entities without a Chinese commercial banking license. PBOC and SAFE regulations require any foreign-invested payment institution to obtain a Payment Business License and SAFE registration to clear RMB and foreign exchange in China. Consequently, an offshore EMI can only act as a supplementary multi-currency wallet for Hong Kong operating companies, not as the primary treasury rail for a Chinese WFOE. Using an unauthorised EMI as the main transaction account will trigger AML downgrade and possible administrative sanction. The viable approach is a Hong Kong treasury entity with the foreign-funded EMI for offshore disbursements, while all onshore RMB obligations are settled via Tier-1 Chinese banks.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: SAFE and PBOC KYC Directive No. 1 require the statutory legal representative (or a senior compliance officer with a notarized power of attorney) of the WFOE to appear physically before the bank's branch compliance officer for the initial onboarding interview. Remote consular proxy opening is generally not permitted for WFOEs because the bank must verify the identity of the ultimate controlling shareholder and assess business substance on the ground. For foreign shareholders located outside China, the bank may accept an apostilled Certificate of Incumbency and a board resolution, but this does not waive the physical interview for the local legal representative. A documentary-only account opening is rarely afforded, and video KYC is accepted only for follow-up updates or product additions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Concealed beneficial ownership and unaudited Hong Kong interposing holding layers
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete corporate organigram of the ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) with passport copies; Hong Kong Companies Registry certificate of incorporation, annual return and register of members; notarised shareholders' resolution designating the WFOE's authorized signatories; a Hong Kong tax representative letter confirming economic substance; and audited financial statements of the intermediate holding company for two years.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-verifiable data sourcing and intellectual property risk in public web scraping operations
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PRC litigation lawyer opinion confirming compliance with Criminal Law Article 285, Cybersecurity Law, Data Security Law and Personal Information Protection Law; signed contracts with data suppliers along with updated API terms of service; robots.txt and scraping permission audit reports; records showing consent and opt-out mechanisms for individual data; and GDPR/CCPA compliance attestation from a third-party security auditor.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cryptocurrency (USDC) payment rails implying insufficient anti-money laundering control
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A documented policy prohibiting third-party or anonymous crypto funding; whitelisted digital wallet addresses signed by the UBO; on-chain KYC/AML attestation from the issuing exchange (e.g., Circle or regulated exchange); concurrent transaction monitoring log with linkage between on-chain transactions and corresponding invoices; and a corporate resolution clearly stating that USDC settlement will only be used for verified customer subscriptions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Benchmark mismatch between projected turnover and requested transactional limits
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A CPA-prepared cash flow reconciliation statement; Stripe settlement reports and API usage metering data for the trailing twelve months; signed commercial contracts with key clients; a pragmatic business plan projecting the scrape-as-a-service revenue; and tax filing summaries with FIT payments to demonstrate realistic operational scale.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The Hong Kong holding company must wire capital into the WFOE's designated Capital Escrow Account at a Tier-1 Chinese bank under the SAFE foreign exchange registration code provided by the local SAFE branch. A wire must reference the payment purpose code for investment funds and align with the registered total investment amount. The WFOE must submit the received notification to the bank together with the Foreign Exchange Verification Form within 30 days, and a certified Chinese CPA must issue a Capital Verification Report within three months to certify the paid-in capital. Funds can then be converted to RMB for business use on a case-by-case basis subject to the registered business scope.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For cross-border trade settlement of software development fees, server hosting costs and API licensing disbursements, the WFOE may use standard SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfers via its domestic bank, provided the corresponding commercial contract, invoice, tax certificate and foreign contract registration are supplied. For larger equipment or raw material procurement on behalf of offshore clients, Commercial Letters of Credit (L/C) at sight or Documentary Collections are advisable to reduce counterparty risk. Alternatively, for settlements with Hong Kong counterparties, the RMB transfer can be routed through the Cross-Border Interbank Payment System (CIPS) to avoid FX cost. Foreign exchange payments require the current account purpose code for digital economy service fees and a SAFE online verification filing prior to remittance.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore RMB forward contracts (deliverable) with licensed Chinese banks for current account exposures
Foreign exchange swaps between RMB and USD for cash flow matching under SAFE approval
FX options via the interbank market cannot be freely used by non-financial corporates; only synthetic forward positions are permitted
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not available onshore; the Hong Kong offshore RMB market can be used while respecting the WFOE's actual foreign debt quota

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 42 days after the anniversary of the company's incorporation date each year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing attracts escalating late fees: HKD 870 if filed within 3 months, HKD 1,740 within 6 months, HKD 2,610 within 9 months, and HKD 3,480 thereafter; prosecution is possible and persistent default may lead to administrative strike-off of the company.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Business Registration Office, Inland Revenue Department, Hong Kong SAR
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than one month after the annual expiry date of the Business Registration Certificate; renewal may be made from one month before that expiry date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Carrying on business after expiry without renewal is an offence, subject to a maximum fine of HKD 5,000 and imprisonment; continued non-renewal may result in deregistration of the Hong Kong business.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department, Hong Kong SAR
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month of the date of issue shown on the Profits Tax Return; customary IRD extensions may apply for certain accounting year ends, but the statutory obligation runs from the issue date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file without reasonable excuse attracts a fine of up to HKD 10,000; if tax is undercharged, an additional penalty of up to three times the undercharged tax may be imposed.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Employer's Return of Remuneration and Pensions (Form BIR56A and supporting IR56 forms)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department, Hong Kong SAR - Employer's Return Unit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month of the date of issue of the Employer's Return, which is normally issued in early April each year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failing to file without reasonable excuse can result in a fine of up to HKD 10,000 and imprisonment; understated employee remuneration may attract additional tax assessments.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR), People's Republic of China - National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually from 1 January to 30 June following the end of the reporting fiscal year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing leads to inclusion on the 'List of Enterprises with Abnormal Operating Conditions', an administrative fine of RMB 5,000 to RMB 30,000, and restrictions on banking credit, government procurement, and market access; persistent default may lead to revocation of the business license.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Annual Settlement and Filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA), People's Republic of China
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 31 May of the calendar year following the tax year, with quarterly provisional payments due within 15 days after each quarter end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment interest accrues at 0.05% per day on unpaid tax; late filing fines range from RMB 2,000 to RMB 10,000; false or fraudulent filings may be penalized by an additional 50% of underpaid tax.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM), People's Republic of China, administered jointly through the SAMR Annual Report Portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually from 1 January to 30 June, aligned with the SAMR enterprise annual report window; no separate filing date applies.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to submit the FIE annual information report results in inclusion on abnormal operation or untrustworthy lists; prolonged non-compliance may trigger administrative enforcement under the Foreign Investment Law, including restrictions on dividend remittance and business activities.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: All Hong Kong private companies, except wholly dormant companies, are legally required to appoint an independent certified public accountant and file audited financial statements; there are no balance-sheet, turnover, or headcount exemptions under the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622). The mainland China WFOE is likewise subject to a mandatory annual audit by a licensed Chinese CPA firm under the PRC Company Law and foreign-invested enterprise accounting regulations; no size threshold exempts a WFOE from audit. Quantitative triggers: none are applicable to this structure; both the Hong Kong holding entity and the mainland China WFOE are audit-required in every accounting period.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Hong Kong entity: Hong Kong Financial Reporting Standards (HKFRS), fully converged with IFRS; eligible private companies may apply HKFRS for SMEs. Mainland China WFOE: PRC Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (ASBE/CAS), substantially converged with IFRS; small enterprises may elect the PRC Small Enterprise Accounting Standards, but the statutory WFOE audit and FIE annual reporting remain compulsory. Consolidated reporting in the Hong Kong parent may use IFRS or HKFRS, while standalone statutory accounts of the WFOE must be prepared under PRC GAAP.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Hong Kong: the company must maintain a Significant Controllers Register (SCR) at its registered office and update it within 7 days of any change; no annual public UBO filing is made to the Companies Registry, but the register must be produced to the Inland Revenue Department and law enforcement upon demand. The Annual Return (NAR1) confirms shareholder and director particulars, and any shareholding transfer must be entered in the Register of Members and reflected in that return. Mainland China WFOE: shareholding transfers must be updated in the shareholder register and filed with the relevant SAMR authorities within 30 days of the change; ultimate beneficial ownership details are reportable under the PRC Anti-Money Laundering regulations, and the FIE annual information report requires confirmation of the controlling party.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$400 to US$1,000 per annum for combined Hong Kong registered office and company secretary services; mainland China registered address maintenance typically US$150 to US$400 per annum.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$3,000 to US$8,000 per annum for a combined Hong Kong parent company audit and mainland China WFOE statutory audit, depending on transaction volume and complexity.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 15% preferential rate for High and New Technology Enterprises; 15% for encouraged industries in Western Regions, Hainan Free Trade Port, and certain free trade zones; 5% effective rate for small low-profit enterprises (taxable income not exceeding CNY 3 million) under the current preferential policy; 100% additional deduction for qualifying R&D expenses; qualified technology transfer income exemption up to CNY 5 million; no general patent box in the PRC, but qualifying integrated circuit and software enterprises may enjoy a two-year exemption followed by three years at 12.5% under the software and IC preferential regime

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: PRC Enterprise Income Tax Annual Return Form A100000 together with supporting schedules including A105000, A107010, A108000, and the Annual Related Party Transactions Report Form G100000; filed electronically through the State Taxation Administration e-Tax / Electronic Tax Bureau portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; quarterly provisional payments and reporting
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual settlement and filing by 31 May of the following calendar year; quarterly provisional returns and payments within 15 days after the end of each quarter; annual transfer pricing contemporaneous documentation deadline is 31 May of the following year

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal identity, unified social credit code, tax resident status, fiscal year, and industry classification
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify the WFOE as a PRC resident enterprise; declare the ultimate H.K. parent as a non-resident controlling party; ensure ISIC 6201 / NAICS 518210 business scope description matches the web scraping and proxy API gateway revenue activities; any inconsistency with the business licence may trigger a tax-risk flag.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Financial statement data: revenue, cost of operations, selling expenses, administrative expenses, financial expenses, asset impairment losses, fair value changes, investment income, operating profit, non-operating income, non-operating expenses, and total accounting profit
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Recognize all cross-border API subscription, data licensing, scraping service, and proxy gateway revenue on an accrual basis; intercompany recharges from the H.K. parent must be supported by substantive contracts and arm's-length pricing; understatement of overseas digital service revenue is a direct audit trigger.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax adjustments: related-party adjustments, thin capitalization, non-deductible expenses, advertising and business entertainment limitations, bad debt write-offs, and special tax adjustment items
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If annual fees paid to the H.K. parent for scraping IP, software algorithms, data delivery, or management services exceed arm's-length benchmarks, enter the mandatory adjustment in Schedule A105000; royalties paid to a zero-substance H.K. shell must be disallowed; excessive debt-to-equity ratios trigger thin capitalization rules under EIT Law Article 46.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income computation, tax-exempt income, non-taxable income, prior-year loss deduction, and adjusted taxable income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The WFOE is taxed on worldwide income; dividend distribution to the H.K. parent does not reduce taxable income; carryforward tax losses may be used for 5 years, except qualifying high-tech enterprises and eligible startups may use a 10-year carryforward; ensure loss records survive any change in business scope.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax rate, tax payable, tax credits, and foreign tax credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply 25% headline rate unless a valid high-tech enterprise certificate supports 15%; apply foreign tax credit for qualified overseas taxes if the WFOE earns foreign-derived income; the H.K. parent's treaty status does not reduce the WFOE's CIT rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prepayments, tax relief, and non-resident dividend withholding declaration
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The WFOE acts as a withholding agent for outbound profit distributions to the H.K. parent; the distribution entry must record the statutory 10% EIT withholding or the 5% China-H.K. DTA rate only after treaty benefit approval; the withholding return is separate from the annual CIT return and must be filed at the time of dividend approval or actual payment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Related party transaction disclosure and economic substance narrative
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose all transactions with the H.K. parent, including royalty, API gateway fee, technical service fee, data sales, cost-sharing, and loan interest; confirm whether the transaction value exceeds the Local File threshold; state the business functions, assets, and risks borne by the WFOE versus the H.K. parent; failure to file Form G100000 is an independent compliance violation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts a penalty of up to CNY 2,000, or CNY 10,000 for serious cases, plus a daily late surcharge of 0.05% of overdue tax under Tax Collection Law Article 32; under-reporting or tax evasion under Article 63 triggers additional tax, interest, and a penalty of 50% to 5 times the tax underpaid; false related-party documentation or intentional omission of cross-border transactions may be recharacterized under Special Tax Adjustment rules and referred to criminal handling when the evaded tax exceeds the statutory criminal threshold.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% statutory dividend withholding tax under PRC EIT Law Articles 3 and 37 for a non-resident enterprise receiving dividends from a PRC-resident WFOE; reduced to 5% under the China-H.K. Double Tax Arrangement where the H.K. parent is the beneficial owner and holds directly at least 25% of the WFOE capital for the 365-day period preceding the dividend payment
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The WFOE or the H.K. parent must file a non-resident treaty benefit application through the State Taxation Administration e-Tax platform before or at the time of distribution; the claimant must obtain a Hong Kong Inland Revenue Department Tax Residency Certificate; provide a Beneficial Ownership self-certification under SAT Public Notice 2018 No. 9; supply board resolutions, shareholding register, bank statements, staffing records, office lease, and CIGA evidence proving the H.K. parent carries on substantive business activity; if approved, the withholding agent applies the 5% DTA rate; if denied, the statutory 10% withholding applies and a refund claim may be pursued within three years under Article 51 of the EIT Law
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT for non-resident enterprises on interest and royalties is 10%; under the China-H.K. DTA the WHT is reduced to 7% for both interest and royalties, provided the recipient is the beneficial owner and the income is not attributable to a permanent establishment in the PRC; the WFOE must withhold at source and file Form F/S with the local tax authority; a H.K. shell with no real business activity cannot claim the 7% treaty rate.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Contemporaneous Local File: annual related-party transactions exceeding CNY 200 million for tangible asset transfers, CNY 100 million for financial asset transfers, CNY 100 million for intangible asset transfers, or CNY 40 million for other transactions; Master File: annual related-party transactions exceeding CNY 1 billion; Country-by-Country Report: MNE group consolidated revenue of CNY 5.5 billion or more in the prior fiscal year
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: PRC substance-over-form and General Anti-Avoidance Rules under EIT Law Articles 47 and 120 allow the tax authority to disregard or recharacterize a transaction lacking reasonable commercial purpose; a H.K. parent claiming treaty benefits must satisfy the Beneficial Ownership requirements of SAT Public Notice 2018 No. 9 and must pass the Principal Purpose Test incorporated through the MLI; under Hong Kong law, the H.K. resident must perform Core Income-Generating Activities in Hong Kong, including decision-making, management, staff, premises, and risk assumption, to support offshore claims and treaty access; a WFOE whose H.K. parent is a nominee vehicle with no real substance will lose the 5% dividend rate and may trigger CFC and anti-treaty-abuse adjustments.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Documentation Failure and Thin Capitalization Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE pays inflated monthly scrape-API, data licensing, and technical service fees to a H.K. parent with no employees, premises, or functional capability, and fails to prepare contemporaneous Local File documentation or file the Annual Related Party Transactions Report; the WFOE reports near-zero profit while the H.K. parent accumulates profits without economic activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: EIT Law Articles 41 and 46 and SAT Public Notice 2016 No. 42 authorize transfer pricing recharacterization and thin capitalization adjustment; Tax Collection Law Article 63 imposes additional tax, daily interest surcharges, and a penalty of 50% to 5 times the underpaid tax; the tax authority may also apply a 5% annual adjustment interest under special tax adjustment rules.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Where the WFOE is found to be a mere conduit and the H.K. parent controls all decisions, the corporate veil may be pierced under PRC Company Law; directors and actual controllers may be jointly and severally liable for the restored taxable income, unpaid tax, and penalties; the legal representative may be blacklisted by the State Taxation Administration, subjected to an exit ban under the Exit-Entry Administration Law, and face criminal investigation under Criminal Law Article 201 for fraudulent tax avoidance if the conduct was intentional.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion Through Fabricated Costs and False Special VAT Invoices
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Directors approve the purchase of false special VAT invoices from ghost vendors labeled as technical consulting and web infrastructure services, inflating deductible costs by CNY 15 million, reducing the WFOE's CIT liability, and creating fake payment trails through cryptocurrency and shell bank accounts that do not match actual scraping-server operations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal Law Article 205 criminalizes the issuance or use of false special VAT invoices, with fines and imprisonment of three to ten years for large amounts and up to life imprisonment for especially huge amounts; Tax Collection Law Article 63 imposes a penalty of 50% to 5 times the underpaid tax plus full recovery of the evaded tax; the WFOE's deductions are disallowed in their entirety.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, the finance director, and the actual controlling shareholder face criminal imprisonment for tax evasion under Criminal Law Article 201, civil restitution of the avoided tax, frozen assets, and personal joint liability under Company Law; the legal representative is blacklisted from leaving China until tax debts are settled; any director who knowingly signed false invoices is treated as a principal offender rather than protected by limited liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: DTA and Beneficial Ownership Fraud Through a Shell H.K. Parent
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE declares and distributes an CNY 80 million dividend to a newly incorporated H.K. company with no office, staff, business records, or risk-management functions; the WFOE applies the 5% China-H.K. DTA withholding rate while the H.K. company contemporaneously forwards the funds to a Macao or China-resident ultimate beneficiary, exposing the arrangement as treaty shopping and beneficial ownership misdeclaration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax authority may deny treaty benefits under the Principal Purpose Test, SAT Public Notice 2018 No. 9, EIT Law Article 47, and the China-H.K. Arrangement's Limitation of Benefits provisions; the WFOE is liable for the additional 10% withholding tax difference, daily late surcharges, and a penalty of 50% to 5 times the under-withheld tax under Tax Collection Law Article 63 or Article 64; false declarations may also trigger criminal fraud liability.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly signed the treaty benefit declaration and dividend resolution may be personally liable for the unpaid withholding tax as withholding-agent responsible persons; the corporate veil may be pierced because the H.K. shareholder is a sham entity used to evade PRC tax, exposing shareholders to civil asset restitution; the legal representative and beneficial owner face a travel ban, blacklisting by tax and customs authorities, and criminal imprisonment for tax evasion under Criminal Law Article 201; H.K. authorities may also object to the H.K. company's registration and strike it off for lack of economic substance.
